fixtures.rationale: The function decodes a query-string age with parseInt and then applies an eligibility rule to it in the same body.
The function decodes a raw JSON body and then computes a domain total from it in the same body.
Reading one payload field and handing the typed value to the domain is exactly what a handler does; the business effect lives in adopt, not here.

The function fetches a storage row, decodes its string total, and applies the loyalty discount rule in the same body instead of mapping the row first and letting a separate function decide the discount.
The function decodes an API date string with Date.parse and then decides expiry against it in the same body.
The function validates a raw payload with Joi and then branches on the validated value's business meaning in the same body.
The function's whole job is mapping a database row shape into a typed object; it applies no business rule.
The handler extracts the typed value from the payload and passes it straight to an injected service, returning that service's result unchanged; the business decision lives in the service, not here.
A typed Date formatted into a string never touches a parse call or an external-shape word, so the function never enters the prefilter at all.
The function only decodes a string-encoded amount into a typed Money value; it applies no business rule.
A typed object literal returned unchanged never touches a parse call or an external-shape word, so the function never enters the prefilter at all.

Splitting a string into a structured name converts one representation into another and returns it; no business rule is applied, so it is translation whichever label the model prefers over domain values.

amounts is already a typed array of Money domain values summed by a plainly named accumulator; nothing in the function touches a parse call or an external-shape word, so it never enters the prefilter at all.

Both order.status and filter.status are already typed Status enum values, and neither parameter name nor body touches a parse call or an external-shape word, so the function never enters the prefilter at all.

payment.amount is declared string on the parameter, so converting it with Number here is decoding a text-encoded value, and the function then applies a business threshold to the result in the same body.
The function decodes a string-encoded environment variable with Number and validates it, throwing when malformed; validating and rejecting malformed input is part of translating, not a business rule.

The function reads a request header, generates and propagates a request id when the caller sent none, and logs once; generating and propagating ids and logging are part of translating, not a business rule.

The function passes the typed payload straight to an injected service and, on a null result, throws an injected not-found error; delegating to an injected collaborator and converting an absent result into an error are both part of translating, not a business rule.
The repository method fetches and maps the storage row, then decides which of several teams the work is filed against; that selection is a business rule living inside the storage adapter.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
